We went here at the end of June and the insect activity was off the charts - my partner and I were being eaten alive. We got caught in some bad weather (we anticipated rain) what we didn’t anticipate was how quickly the trail floods. 
Even before that; we came upon a semi demolished bridge, half submerged boardwalks, and mud that pulls you in if you happen to land in it. 

If the weather was a bit nicer I would have enjoyed the hike a lot more since the trail has a fair mix of features (vegetation, views, changing terrain) that gives you a great idea of the many ecosystems in Algonquin. 

The hike itself isn’t hard just make sure you wear waterproof gear and lots of bug spray or come when it’s been dry a couple of days.

Wow, this is an amazing hike.  The Trail Guide was a big value-add in understanding the varied landscape along the trail.  In particular how Bat Lake, one of the most acidified lakes in the Park (pH ~4.8), was probably like that well before the industrial age. And how that acidification, which allows no fish to exist in it , in fact allows different species like salamanders to thrive.  

I thought I was doing well along this moderately challenging Trail.  Then, while enjoying the view from the bench at the Lookout just past Post #7, a young couple walking their 11-year-old dog caught up to me.  Now that was a reality check, and some perspective on how challenging the trail really is .

Such a stunning view of Algonquin. It was a great trail overall that allowed you to see so many different landscapes and ecosystems. Bogs, forests, marshy wetlands - this trail had it all. A must see.

Very nice trail with a variety of terrain, flat, stairs, board walks & inclines, the small view point & Bat lake. Shouldn’t be rated as an “easy trail” though, I hike regularly & this should be rated moderate. Will be back for sure!
Great trail!  Even with humidity being high, hardly any bugs.  We saw a Toad and a Pine Martin.
Really peaceful and beautiful hike. Trails are great and hardly any bugs.
great hike. First part is beautiful with streams etc. Some deadfall that you have to go over and a few wet patches. The two docks at Bat lake were both underwater. No bugs overall a nice hike.
Generally easy trail but need to watch your feet due to lots of roots. Few nice lookouts.
Very well marked trail, muddy in some parts but nothing you can’t avoid. One big hill and otherwise a great hike and easy access for the dogs to swim
I think this is my favourite trail in Algonquin.  Hiked it on a foggy/rainy day and it just blew me away.  One steep climb that's not too hard, and the rest of the trail is fairly easy.
The first bit was so beautiful! I would do it again just for the beginning of the trail.
Some parts seemed very washed out, but otherwise a very pleasant walk.

We hiked the trail in reverse ; the first section was ok scenery wise until the boardwalk over the lake which was very serene. The hike up to the look out was a good work out. The second half of the trail with water falls, jagged and moss covered  rock face was great. A very scenic hike all around
Nice trail! Nice lookout, muddy in some parts but not too bad. I’d say this was easy in terms of difficulty.
Great trail with lots of nice views, but there were many muddy/wet spots

If the parking lot is empty, swing by and enjoy it for as long as you can, 
personally prefer going back wards (blue markers) as in the beginning you're treated to a few water features and sounds of water. 
enjoy,
It was a great hike but the mosquitoes were vicious! Even with bug spray each of us left with at least 10 bites each.
mostly uphill to start and narrow. view is pretty but limited seating. one bench so prepare to wait if you want to sit a while.
amazing views, not difficult, lots of scenery
Great lookout and lake, but spiders and mosquitoes are constant the whole trail. Bring bug spray and a stick to clear webs.
Great
Peaceful. Some hills and rocky surfaces to traverse. Amazing lookout at Bat lake. Saw lots of animal scat. Not sure what animal. Didn’t see any wildlife. Great trail.
Took us 2 hours and 40 mins to complete. Icy and muddy uphill and downhill trail. More of a moderate trail and has nice lookouts!

Great trail.. First 3km is moderate with a steady climb up to the lookout and the final stretch downhill and I would call this portion easy..

Still snow and ice on the trail so ice cleats would be beneficial for some parts.  Trail maintenance has not been done yet so there are a number of trees down on the trail.
Spring at it's finest, no other people on the trail and mostly melting compacted ice. Had an amazing hike playing Foothole roulette the whole way! Recommend for a short but worthwhile hike.
very slippery this time of year. a few nice little ponds and a lookout.

I would highly recommend this hike! I would rank it moderately difficult at this time of the year and be careful of the icy spots. Many elevation changes kept it spicy, a great view at the lookout point and lake views along the way were breathtaking. Did not see any wildlife today but perhaps another day. Parking pass $18.00 when you come in the park and lot is right at trail head.
Beautiful trail. Had a couple icy spots but not bad. Nice lookout
Very beautiful.

A great trail for winter hiking. An easy trail in normal conditions becomes a moderate trail in the winter. A lot of canopy cover with the trail bringing you to 3-4 open wilderness areas and spectacular lookout with a bench. It took us roughly 2.5 -3 hours to complete in snowy conditions. Recommended.
Very nice winter hike. Easier if you do it clockwise.
Nice winter walk, not many hills. Enjoy!
Beautiful in the winter. Saw jack rabbit, pine marten and river otter.
Lovely winter hike with different landscapes and views (rocks with icicles, frozen lakes and rivers, trees). Several benches placed throughout. Was more like 7km though.

The trail was beautiful.   Wonderfull surprise at mid-way point.  Snowshoes helped on climbs and descents but overall very manageable with boots.   There are lots of nice older Pines to see.  also. there is a huge rock on top of the mountain...
Great winter hike!!!
Beautiful during the winter :) bring warm shoes!
Took my family two hours to complete. Lots of different scenery and many chipmunks running around. It is a bit slippery on the boardwalk. Mud is hardened. Nice view of the lake.
Great trail, beautiful scenery. Little muddy at times, take a change of shoes for the car. Does have a few good inclines.

Not a bad trail! Lucked out today and got the trail to myself! Pretty muddy so I would recommend hiking boots. The frost saved us a bit with the mud and most muddy areas you could avoid. Not bad as far as hiking, pretty easy trail and the elevation doesn’t kill you. 
Would be a good trail in the summer with los of shad, and not to bad exercise wise.

Scenic trail through the forest with pretty waterfalls and a great lookout point, plus some boardwalks through marsh areas.

I only gave this a 4 because of the conditions. Being late October, there's a lot of mud. Most of it you can avoid but there are a few bits that are tricky to navigate around, mostly the steep decline around the 3k mark - going downhill in thick, slippery mud is a bit nerve-wracking! There are the usual roots and stones, which are a bit harder to spot under all the leaves (I went in late Oct) plus the boardwalks are a bit slippery when wet. Mind your step, wear good shoes/boots and you'll be fine (and bring a change of footwear).

missed the colours but a great hike the
 trail was a touch boggy
Not as muddy as nearby trails currently. One nice small lookout, a couple boardwalks. Very nice waterfall to walk along.
really enjoyed this trial. Found the second half of it to be less scenic but still a great Trail for hiking nonetheless. Completed in 1.5 hours, the map suggests 3.5 hours.
Great hike, nice trails with a variety of vegetation lots of pine trees for a change. started the recording about 300-500 meters into it, sorry.
Nice trail with a pretty pond fed stream and several small cascading waterfalls.  May be a little strenuous in spots for new or infrequent hikers.

This trail was so pretty and the lookout was amazing. I recommend doing it at the trail head direction rather than backwards because if you do, there is a spot where the incline is quite strenuous. And yeah, saw a snake and lots of chipmunks that were none too pleased to see us lol
Great trail! Pretty dry in most areas. Boardwalks are in good shape
Beautiful,  peaceful hike. Watch out for the Gardner snakes! We saw 2 right off the path. Breathtaking views of the fall colours.
Lots of different type of trees and fungi around!
Easy hike with interesting fungi. Saw a Canada Jay and a cruising hawk.
Trail was in great condition overall. Particularly interesting to see the different forest ecosystems all so close to each other.
Great hike, with one big incline otherwise very easy. Lovely creek and a great scenic look out.  Definitely recommend. A little muddy but not a big deal.
Great trail! My husband lost his shoe in the mud, that was super funny! Beautiful bridges and views!
Rocky and steep at points.  Some of the stairs have been washed away.
great afternoon activity!
Nice easy hike through the forest. Very nice but nothing spectacular. Bat Lake and Davey’s Bog were pretty!

I am not an experienced hiker and it rained all night last night so some of this trail was challenging.  I definitely would not describe it as easy.  I would considerate more moderate.  But...we did it, along with our grandchildren ages 6 and 10. We're going to be sore tonight but this was a very pretty trail and well worth the aches and pains!
some good hills and a beautiful stream running down the hills.
Nice scenic trail!! Be prepared for the bugs if you plan on going in Summer. It is clearly marked and well maintained.
Awesome
Great trail. Easier side despite the mini climb. A few roots and rocky spots but a nice quick walk.

Great trail, first half was gorgeous, second half less exciting. Very steep decline and was very muddy at this part making it a bit more challenging. Wouldn’t rate as easy but still a good shorter hike if you’re looking for something without a major climb.
Great Trail. A little bit of everything. Verity of forest, marsh, boardwalk, with a lookout, lake views. One of my fav trails in the park.
Beautiful trail. Loved the stream near the beginning..lush and green with large rocks. I hiked it today right before and into a storm and it felt like I was in a rainforest with the humidity!
A perfect moderate morning trail with beautiful lakes and shaded Forrest. I recommend long pants/shirt for bugs.

My family and I were on this trail today. I  Loved this trail but children were trying to escape the mosquitoes. It rained last night which might have caused the mosquitoes. The trail is quite steep and at the top a very nice look out, loved to board walk except the mosquitoes were not friendly.  You need to be in good shape if you plan to go on this trail, I have been hiking for sometime and will not consider this trail quite easy. Overall, I loved the trail..
Beautiful trail with a nice lookout.
I enjoyed this trail but saw 2 snakes  nice a quite nice view on the top

Absolutely loved this trail.  The first half is a steady incline climb for about 2.4 km.  Not difficult if your a regular hiker or in half decent shape.  The first is old growth and beautiful.  reaching the summit and looking out at the lake is beautiful.  You are a good 300 metres above the lake and the view is spectacular.  The hike down is easy with the aid of several staircases.  Other then that it's outstanding and recommended.
Good trail in the winter time and great time with my 7 year old
great trail was -20 the day we went hiked to frozen waterfall and back. would do this again.
It was slightly icy in some bits, very compacted trail. Fabulous hike! Go clockwise around because you get to see some amazing ice waterfalls! We took our dogs and they loved the trail!
Good trail just completed last week. The path was snow covered but walked on so easy. No icy spots yet. Can get icy downhill later in the season. Took 1.5 hours to do the trail. Beautiful!
Great for kids.
Really nice!

Essentially a nice walk in the woods.  This trail is very well maintained, and therefore very easy to hike.  The path is wide, with few elevations changes you'll notice.  There's isn't a lot to look at - perhaps just the acidic lake and a small look out - but it's a nice place for a quiet walk.
The park believes the trail will take 3.5 hours, when in reality it's closer to 2.  Probably a lot less if you're a frequent hiker.  I took 2 hours today with several spots spending a few minutes to take pictures.

We enjoyed the trail, but it probably shouldn't be listed as an 'easy' trail. there are a couple of challenging descents, and one in particular with large precarious stones where you can easily turn an ankle if you're not steady and deliberate. Bring your most potent insect repellant... we found the incessant swarms of mosquitos and flies somewhat tiresome...This is even after generous and repeated applications of DEET. The best thing about the trail was the superb eco-friendly ecology and biology readings contained in the thin Algonquin Park pamphlet that accompanies this trail. it was very well done.

There are so many vegetation changes along this trail as well as (at present) some conservation assessments!  The guidebook does a beautiful job noting them, and I think the route would be perfectly suited to kids interested in nature and science.  However, it was extremely buggy at some point, to the point of swarming mosquitoes, possibly related to the marsh and lake.

We did this trail in 2.5 hours at a leisurely pace with a lot of stopping at the posts to read up on the trail from the provided booklet and to take pictures. Still a partially submerged dock on bat lake and of course, the bugs were swarming us (crazy mosquitoes) but it is so beautiful and rewarding!

Most of the lower parts of the trail were still very snowy/icy and very slippery. The docks for viewing the lake a currently submerged so we weren't able to go out and look. Would definitely be more enjoyable once it warms up some more to help melt the ice.

Careful in the springtime with this trail, the ice can be treacherous!

The section that climbs up to Jack Lake through Jack Creek's gully is incredibly beautiful, and challenging in places. 

Lots of great views, and the interpretative trail guide was interesting.

Nice little hike! Some great little streams and mini waterfalls. Lots of little bridges and crossings. Half way there is a nice lookout! Would recommend. I took about 2-2.5 hours but spent a lot of time taking photos. If you don’t stop it would probably take 1.5 hour to hike.

The lower parts of the hike are still under a lotnof snow and ice! If you do it, then go in the morning. After lunch the ice is getting very slippery! But very beautiful trail! Some parts around the lake are under water but you can easily go around! Took me 1h45min to complete it.
Clean. Moderate.
Beautiful, slightly demanding, walk in the winter.
Very nice walk in the winter.
Beautiful look out over the lake, different foliage and terrain throughout the walk.

Beautiful mix of scenery. I ran this trail with my dogs in the early spring, lots and lots of ice and where there wasn't ice the was mud, but that's when you get when you run in the woods in early spring! I would imagine this trail would have a lot of bugs once the ground thaws.. but this is one of my favourites so far:)

I almost die at this trail. In an early May’s night, I came to No.10 stick- that is, the bank of Bat lake. The lake is iced, so I don’t know the road is cross the lake or along the lake. I went cross the lake and finally lost the way. Luckily, I didn’t fall into ice lake. Thanks Load.
Hiked the trail in December with snowshoes (though they were not really needed). Nice variety of things to see from different forests, to ice formations, to scenic views.
We did this trail in the winter of 2017 (February) with our daughters 4 and 3, very scenic trail . Would definitely recommend hiking this loop in the winter weather
Nice little walk but a lot of Moskitos.
Great view and cool boardwalks. Took us 2.5 hours at a moderate pace and a few breaks for photos and sites.
Great trail. Lots of interesting features. Fine lookout. Not too long or difficult.
Love this trail. Perfect length, beautiful and diverse scenery.
my favorite trail in algonquin park, different terrain and views on this trail
Really cool hike!  Changes in different terrain.  Beautiful views.  A nice lookout point from top of hill with look out below to bodies water and all that jazz.
A great kid friendly trail. Do it three times a year in different seasons.
This was a very nice trail with a variety of scenery from creeks and ponds to outlooks.
